Commentary.Commentary: The hosts, on the other hand, would be disappointed with their performance. Apart from Dean Elgar and Rassie van der Dussen, no one got going. They were 40 for 3 at one stage and then a comeback of sorts happened. A 117-run stand between Elgar And van der Dussen made everyone think that they were in control. However, once Elgar and Quinton de Kock threw away their wickets, the Proteas never recovered and conceded a valuable lead of 46 runs. The South African bowlers have a tough task ahead as they need to pick up wickets at regular intervals in order to get back in this game. Can they make a comeback or will the visitors run away with the match? Join us in a while to find out.

26 balls is all it took for the English bowlers to take the two remaining South African wickets. They have put in an incredible effort in the field as they go back to the pavilion with a lead of 46 runs. Anderson and Broad were terrific from the start. They reduced the hosts to 40/3 but then Rassie van der Dussen and Dean Elgar combined to form a terrific stand of 117 runs. In that period, 12 No Balls were not picked by the on-field umpire. However, when van der Dussen was dismissed but the on-field umpire then referred upstairs to check for a No Ball and Rassie survived. Stokes dropped a catch too. It looked like South Africa would make them pay. But once Elgar fell, it was a procession as they lost their last six wickets for just 32 runs. James Anderson picked up a 5-fer, his 28th in Test cricket, surpassing the record for an English player set by legend, Sir Ian Botham. However, it was Stuart Broad who was the pick of the bowlers as he kept on bowling perfect lines and lengths throughout Day 2.

OUT! CAUGHT! 5-fer for James Anderson, his 28th in Test cricket! Brilliant from Stokes as well as he takes a stunning catch in the slip cordon. This is a terrific ball from James Anderson. A good length ball outside off, inducing the drive from Anrich Nortje. The batter obliges but he manages just an outside edge on it. The ball flies to the right of first slip and to the left of second slip. Stokes from second slip dives to his left and takes a superb catch to end the South African innings. Stokes takes his 5th catch of this innings and becomes the first outfield English player to do so. All smiles for the England players as they return to the pavilion.

Another bumper around off this time, Anrich ducks under it comfortably.

Would have been gone for all money! There was no run there but both the batters went for it. Good length ball on off, Vernon gets a thick edge towards gully and takes off for a run. Pope there dives to his right and gathers the ball. Pope throws it at the keeper's end but misses the stumps. Had he hit, Nortje would have been out by a mile. He was not even in the frame as the replays rolled in. Wondering why would Philander want to take a single off the first ball and give Nortje the strike so soon in his innings?
Fullish outside off, Anrich shoulders arms to it.
Fuller one on off, Vernon pushes it to deep cover and takes a single. Nortje has to survive one ball of Broad now.
On off, defended off the back foot.
On a length on off, Philander looks to defend but goes off the outside edge and rolls towards gully.
On a length outside off, hitting a crack on the pitch, causing it to bounce a little more. Philander looks to punch but misses it altogether due to the extra bounce on it.
BEATEN! Wild drive from Philander! Full delivery outside off, Philander looks to play an expansive drive to this one but fails to get any bat on it.
Stuart Broad to bowl from the other end.
Yes, he can! Anderson bowls a good length ball outside off, Nortje leaves this ball alone.
Anrich Nortje is the last man in and he will be facing the hat-trick ball against James Anderson. Can he survive against it?

OUT! CAUGHT! What a start to Day 3 for England! That is some bowling from James Anderson! On a length, outside off, nipping away. Rabada looks to defend this with little to no foot movement and the ball takes a faint outside edge back to Buttler who makes no mistake. Anderson appeals and the umpire raises his finger. A wicket off the last ball of Day 2 and now a wicket off the first ball on Day 3. Anderson is on fire.

We are all set to begin Day 3. Vernon Philander and the new batsman, Kagiso Rabada make their way out to the middle. They are still 54 runs behind. Can they take the lead? We will soon find out. The England players are also out in the middle. James Anderson will finish his over.

South Africa ended Day 2 on a bad note. They lost 4 wickets for 24 runs in the latter stages of the day and have Vernon Philander as the only batsman who can grind out some runs for them. They still trail by 54 runs and Philander would be hoping that the two remaining batters support him out in the middle and get the team as close to England's score. The visitors, on the other hand, would want to get the two remaining wickets as soon as possible and then swell their lead to give the home team a tough target. However, on Day 2 itself we could see some dust coming off the surface and that would be exciting for Keshav Maharaj. Both sides' batting has been average and when England come to bat, it will surely not be easy on this wicket. Stay tuned for all the action as a crucial day for both these sides lie ahead!
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

England had 1 wicket left entering into Day 2 but a set batsman as well in Ollie Pope. South Africa have 2 wickets left going into Day 3 but it is going to be Vernon Philander who has to control the batting on Sunday. Rabada and Nortje are no pushovers but they need to bat sensibly. Join us back on January 5, 2020 at 10.30 am local (0830 GMT) for all the action. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

54 is the drift between England and South Africa at the moment. On this pitch, it looks a bit too much for the Proteas. They need to try and get as close as possible to the visitors' total and make this a one-inning shootout. Don't forget, the hosts are going to be batting last on this pitch. Would not want to chase anything above 150.

Now, to England's bowling. Cannot really criticize the bowlers. They bowled their hearts out. But Joe Root's captaincy was questionable. He just allowed the game to drift away in the second session, allowing easy singles. Then, he changed tactics in the third, stopping the runs, which eventually resulted in the flow of wickets. Anderson got 3 but the pick of the day was Stuart Broad who was relentless. Sam Curran showed the value of cutters in this format as well, getting rid of the dangerous de Kock and van der Dussen.

A reminder of the opening session, where England did not make too many runs this morning but managed to get three Protea wickets which also included that of the skipper Faf. The Saffas were in trouble at 40/3 but then Elgar, van der Dussen, Stuart Broad and Ben Stokes bailed them out. The first two forged a nice partnership, while Broad got Rassie's wicket but overstepped. Stokes, on the other hand, missed a catch of van der Dussen as well.

It was the third session on Day 1 which rocked England. It was the third session again on Day 2 which rocked the Proteas. It started with Dean Elgar, throwing his wicket out of nowhere, just like Ben Stokes did last evening. Quinton de Kock tried to play a quickfire knock, just like he did in the previous Test but he lived by the sword and died by it. He added 20 in just 26 balls but his wicket opened the floodgates. South Africa slipped from 191/5 to 215/8 in 63 balls. Advantage England.

What an action-packed day. Does anyone even remember what happened in the second session? People were yawning, shoulders were drooping, defensive fields were set and Elgar was batting. Normally, when he bats, he causes a lot of frustration to the fielding side. Because it appears as if he is being beaten but he never gets out. That second session saw 81 runs being scored without a wicket lost. At Tea, South Africa, 3 down and just 128 behind, yes, JUST 128 behind, were looking in full control to have this deficit down to 30-40 odd by Stumps. But well, this thought just jinxed them.

Whoa! What happened? What is it in that last 15 overs in the day? Day 1 saw 4 wickets fall for 13 runs in 43 balls. Day 2 sees 3 wickets fall for 15 runs in 53 balls. Dim light? Anxiety of finishing the day safely? No idea. It has hurt both teams but it is England who find themselves on top now.

OUT! CAUGHT! A wicket to end the day! That is a terrific ball. It ends a brilliant session for England. On a length on off, nipping in, Maharaj looks to flick but it goes off the inside edge onto the pads. It then lobs off to third slip where Sibley takes the catch running forward. Anderson first appeals for LBW but then sees Dominic Sibley taking the catch. He appeals again and Kumar Dharmasena, the on-field umpire gives it out signaling that it has hit the inside edge. STUMPS ON DAY 2, SA TRAIL BY 54!

Stuart Broad is back on. 14-5-34-2 so far.

Pretorius looks to push at it but it goes off the outside edge to second slip. Stokes, ohh Stokes, drops one and takes another. He moves to his right and pouches it with both hands. This was a tough catch and Stokes has done wonderfully well. Wait, the sideways replay rolls in and it shows that Ben had caught it with just one hand. The left hand came to it late. For a change, luck favouring England.

Pretorius looks to defend but takes the outside edge going towards second slip. Stokes usually does not drop those but this one he puts one down. He bends on his knees to his left, gets two hands to it but does not hold on. Probably he was worried whether the ball will carry to him or not.
The second new ball is due now and it has been taken immediately. James Anderson is back on. 14-6-28-1, are his figures so far.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another one bites the dust! Sam Curran does it again for England. Stokes takes a brilliant catch at second slip. Indecision costs Rassie his wicket. He is not sure whether to come forward or not but his basic foot movement is to plant his left foot forward, almost like a reflex action. Now, this is a good length ball outside off and van der Dussen has his left foot planted across. When you do that, it is very difficult to leave balls. The cherry is a touch wide but RvdD has already made up his mind to run this down to third man. Then, when he sees the line, he thinks he can leave it alone. But alas, it is too late. The ball lands and then bounces a touch high. Van der Dussen is in no man's land, just hanging his bat with its face open. The ball takes the outside edge and flies behind. Ben Stokes at slip number 2 dives to his right and takes an excellent catch with both hands. Rassie has to go after playing an excellent knock. South Africa needed him to stay till the end tonight. The deficit is reading 69 and there are still 9 overs left in the day.

Curran's change in pace has done in de Kock here. He rolls his fingers on the ball and lands it on a length outside off. Quinton is early into his shot as he looks to heave and gets a leading edge. It goes high up in the air towards mid off. James Anderson moves to his left from mid off and takes a simple catch. QdK is dejected and looks at the ground before walking off. Has this game opened up again? The deficit is 78. We might be in for a shout regarding a one-inning shootout.

OUT! CAUGHT! Ho ho ho! Are we dreaming? No, we are not! A wicket indeed has fallen. And this time, IT IS NOT A NO BALL. A poor shot from Elgar. Very rarely do we see him doing this but he has thrown it away after playing an excellent innings. He and van der Dussen were running away with the game and this might just bring the visitors back in it. Bess floats this one up outside off, Elgar strides forward and looks to lift it over mid off. However, the ball is not that full to be hit on the rise. He is already through his shot and there is extra bounce on that one. Hence, he does not time it well and it goes high up in the air. Root moves back from mid off and takes the catch. Not easy to catch those. A 100 was there for the taking for Elgar but it was not to be. Elgar is disappointed and looks up to the skies as trudges back to the pavillion. So what is the deficit? 112. Can England get another before it trickles into double digits? Sorry, cannot say trickles. Because the man coming in next will not allow the run rate to trickle down.

We are back for the final session of the day. South Africa are going along nicely and they will look to get closer to the lead. Dean Elgar and Rassie van der Dussen make their way out to the middle. The England players are also out in the ground. Can England pick up further wickets? Dominic Bess will start after the break.
... Day 2, Session 3 ...
33 overs are left in the day. Can England at least break this stand? Join us back at 3.30 pm local (1330 GMT).

Paras 2 and 3 were all South Africa. Now, England. Is everything lost? Do they get the feeling that the whole world is against them? Luck not going their way, catches not being taken... wickets not coming... what do they do? BELIEVE. Just do a bit of a flashback and check what happened last evening. The bowling has not been bad that much but the patience is being tested. South Africa were enormously patient on Friday and were rewarded. England just need to hang around. But yes, they need to stop those silly easy singles. Just too many easy runs on offer.

Gritty. Ugly. Awkward. That is Dean Elgar's defense. But who would care if he is scoring runs? He has hung in there, seen three partners walk off, got some blows on his body but has been undeterred. He has reached 77 now and his century might go a long way in South Africa getting a sizeable lead. The deficit is 128 now - so a good session should see the Saffas reduce it down to the 40s at least by Stumps.

When the rub of the green goes your way, you get all kinds of luck. Rassie van der Dussen is experiencing that at the moment. First, he got a reprieve by a Stuart Broad no ball on 16. Then, he survived a dropped catch by Ben Stokes on 43. He has soldiered on to 46 and will be determined to make the most of his luck now.

A session which could have gone England's way. A session which should have gone England's way. But due to their own mistake, they find it going to their opponents. This is a sort of wicket where one brings two and the visitors did get three quickly in the first session. But in the second, when they got Rassie van der Dussen caught behind, Broad had overstepped and since then, luck has gone against them.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler with an ugly, awkward stance. THAT WILL BE TEA ON DAY 2, SA TRAIL BY 128!

Aha! The hadada is here! Shaun Pollock on air says that it is the same bird which has come on both the days and is pecking at the worms. Teaching the value of persistence and patience to the human beings playing this game of cricket.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Down the leg side, Elgar misses his flick and the ball goes off his pads towards square leg. A leg bye taken.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full again, around off, Elgar brings his bat down at the last moment to defend.
Full and just outside off, watchfully defended back to the bowler.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and around middle, pushed towards short mid-wicket.
100-RUN STAND IS UP! Slowly and surely, South Africa are making themselves comfortable in the driver's seat. Around middle, rucked through square leg for a run.
There he was, chasing a wide one. Full and outside off, hits the footmarks, generates a puff of dust, Elgar looks to drive but misses.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and down the leg side, flicked towards short mid-wicket.
Around off, pushed back with a loose bottom hand.
Full and outside off, driven straight to short extra cover.
Around middle, worked towards short mid-wicket.

Full on middle, Dean pushes it with soft hands towards short mid-wicket. First, he asks his partner to wait, then, when he sees the fielder misfield, calls for two. But later, he sees Stuart Broad get across to his left from mid on and shouts a loud NO. So just a single in the end.

FOUR! That is really good work. Takes the partnership to 98. A half tracker, around middle, coming at a very nice height for the batsman, around tummy high, Elgar does not miss out. Swivels and pulls it through square leg for a boundary. It is very important that England sustain the pressure built up by Anderson.
Full and outside off, Elgar comes forward and blocks.
Sam Curran returns. 6-1-27-0 so far.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Down the leg side, flick shot missed.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Mike Haysman on air informs us that since Lunch 12 NO BALLS HAVE NOT BEEN CALLED! Boy, are the umpires relying too much on the third umpire? Perhaps on checking when a wicket goes down?
Outside off, punched through the covers. The batsmen take the second on the throw and a better one could have had Elgar at the bowler's end.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, punched off the back foot for a single. That was uppish, but well wide of the diving short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, van der Dussen comes forward to defend but the ball takes the outside edge. Does not carry to gully.
Full and outside off, Rassie pushes this with a loose bottom hand and the ball goes uppishly, but well wide of the bowler, towards mid off.
That nips back in off the deck, Rassie looks to defend but the ball cuts him into half. Beats the bat and hits the pad.
Outside off, pushed through point for a single to get to 70.
Outside off, punched off the back foot for a single. The stand moves to 90 now. South Africa trail by 139.
Full and outside off, left alone.
Full and straight, driven back to Root.
Full and around middle now, pushed back to Joe again.
A bit of round-arm from Joe Root, full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, punched straight to cover.
Closer than the previous one, left alone again.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
ROOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOT goes the crowd. The skipper has decided to introduce himself. 20 minutes to go to Tea.
That is a snorter. On a length outside off, van der Dussen feels for it but the ball suddenly kicks up after pitching. Just about beats the outside edge. A testing over from Jimmy.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On a good length outside off, defended awkwardly.
Full and just outside off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, left alone.

EDGED, DROPPED! Ben Stokes, off all the people. Anderson does the hard work, bowls it on a length outside off and makes Rassie go for the drive. The outside edge is taken and it goes to second slip. A dive is required from the fielder and Ben Stokes does dive. Goes one-handed. Now, a catch needs to be taken and Stokes takes it too! But just when he takes the catch with a dive to his right, his right elbow hits the ground and the ball pops out. Stokes has his hands on his head. If looks could kill, Anderson has the 'Meet-me-after-office' type one.
On middle, pushed towards the bowler.
Full again, watchfully blocked out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
Full and around off, pushed towards long on for a single.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Wide outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, that stays low, van der Dussen brings his bat down in time to defend.
Almost a yorker, outside off, pretty full, Elgar digs it out.
Thrown up outside off, driven away from his body, through the covers, for one.
Fired in from around the wicket on middle, van der Dussen blocks it in a hurry.
There is another one. On middle and leg, now Elgar pushes this towards long on for a run.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on for a single. Sorry, long on. For some reason, Joe Root is offering these easy singles.

On off, pushed to the cover fielder.

Floated ball on middle, Elgar pushes it down to long on and crosses over for a single.
Fuller delivery on middle, Rassie pushes it to mid on for nothing.
On a length on off, van der Dussen defends it to point.
On off, defends it off the back foot.
Fuller one outside off, moving in. Rassie lets the ball go to the keeper.

JUST SHORT! Stokes signals it has not carried! Brilliant delivery on off, Rassie van der Dussen looks to defend it out but takes the thick outside edge. It goes towards Stokes at second slip and he dives to his left and collects. There is some excitement but Stokes gets up and signals it has bounced in front of him. He is having all the luck in this game so far.
Back of a length delivery on off, Rassie hops and defends it to cover.
Loopy delivery outside off, Rassie leans forward and drives it through covers for a single.
Flatter delivery on middle, whipped to square leg.
Full on off, pushed to cover.
Tossed up ball on middle, Rassie defends it out.
Full delivery on middle and leg, Elgar pushes it down to long on for a run.
Floated ball on off, Elgar pushes it to short cover.
OHH! Fuller delivery outside off, moving in a little. Rassie makes a good leave to this one.
On a length on middle, Rassie works it to mid-wicket.
Back of a length delivery on off, Rassie hops and defends it off the back foot. Anderson stumbles on his followthrough.
On a length on middle and leg, Rassie defends it to the leg side.

Anderson returns with a good length ball outside off, Elgar lets the ball through to the keeper.

Tossed up delivery outside off, Elgar pushes it past the diving fielder towards deep cover for a single.
Loopy delivery on middle, Elgar defends it out to the off side.
Flatter delivery on middle, Elgar whips it to square leg.
On middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Floated on off, Elgar pushes it to cover.
Drinks!
On middle, Dean works it to the leg side and crosses over for a single.
Short of a length on middle, Rassie looks to flick but gets hit on the pads. It goes towards the leg side and a leg bye is taken.
On a length on middle, Rassie defends it back to the bowler.
Good length ball on middle, Rassie works it to deep mid-wicket and takes another couple before the fielder can clean it up from deep mid-wicket.

Loopy delivery on off, Dean defends it to point.
On off, defended it to the off side.

Floated ball on middle, van der Dussen pushes it down to long on for a single.
There is a slight halt in play as Elgar might have hurt himself after that dive in the previous over.
On off, defended out to the bowler.
Fullish ball outside off, Elgar leaves it alone.
Short of a length on middle, Rassie pulls it to the leg side for a single.

Close! Full delivery on off, Elgar pushes it to cover-point and takes off for a quick run. The fielder comes across and then has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Had he hit, Elgar would have been in though as the dive he made would have saved him. He seems to have hurt himself in the process.
Good length ball on the pads, Rassie works it to deep square leg and takes a run. The replays show that is another no ball from Stokes but not given. Horrendous umpiring.
Short delivery around middle and leg, Elgar pulls it to deep square leg and crosses over for a single.
Flighted ball on middle, Rassie is solid in defense.
Floated on middle, Rassie blocks it out.
FOUR! That's an excellent shot from Rassie van der Dussen. Floated ball outside off, Van der Dussen takes a good stride forward and drives it through extra cover for a boundary.
Looped up ball on off, defended out solidly.
Fuller one outside off, van der Dussen pushes it to cover.
Tossed up delivery on middle and leg, Rassie works it to mid-wicket.
OUCH! That is nasty! Short delivery on middle, Elgar hops to defend but gets hit on the gloves. It just bounces short of the first slip fielder. No harm done.
Back of a length ball on middle, Elgar hops and blocks it to Stokes.
Good length ball down the leg side, Elgar looks to flick but misses it.
Fullish on middle, Elgar works it through mid-wicket and picks up a couple. Broad hares after it and collects it. 100 up for the hosts.
Short of a length ball on middle, Rassie pulls it to deep square leg and crosses over for a single.
Back of a length on off, Rassie camps back and blocks it to cover.
On middle, pushed back to the bowler off the front foot.
Tosses this one up on middle, Rassie looks to defend but it goes off the inside edge which goes towards square leg. A single taken.
Flatter delivery outside off, Elgar pushes it to deep cover and crosses over for a single.
Fullish on middle, Elgar plays it wide of the bowler, towards mid on. No run.

Full delivery outside off, Rassie shoulders arms.
Good length ball on off, pushed to point.
Outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Lovely from Rassie van der Dussen. Fullish ball to start from Stokes. Van der Dussen makes a good stride forward and creams the drive through extra covers for a boundary. It is uppish for a while but it is in the gap. The replays show that Stokes had overstepped by a big margin but it was not given. Wonder what is the umpire doing out there. It happened in South Africa's first innings as well.
Ben Stokes is back on.
Landed outside off, a puff of dust is emanated as the ball lands on the rough generated from the footmarks, Elgar lets it go.
Tossed up again, Rassie leans and pushes this through the covers for a single.
Around middle, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and tossed up outside off, smothered away.
Full and around middle, van der Dussen drives this straight back but Bess dives to his right and makes a half-stop, parrying the ball to short mid-wicket.
Landed outside off, spinning in, worked strai9ght to short mid-wicket.
Dominic Bess is back on. 4-0-10-0 so far.
Full delivery on off, Dean pushes it to cover.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Good length around off, Elgar looks to defend but it goes off the inside edge almost rolling on to stumps. Elgar though, gets his bat in between and pushes it away.
Good length ball outside off, van der Dussen drives it through covers for three before  the fielder can come across and clean it up. 50 run stand is up between the two.

OUT! CAUGHT! No it's not! It is a NO BALL and Broad returns the gift which Rabada gave in the first innings. This was a peach of a delivery though from Broad. Good length delivery around off, Rassie van der Dussen looked to defend it off the back foot but the ball suddenly got a lift. The batsman could do nothing and just managed a glove back to the keeper. Buttler pouched it safely. The umpire gave it out and Rassie started walking. But wait, he was told to stay back as the on-field umpires wanted to check for the no ball. The replas rolled in and it showed that Broad had overstepped by a big margin! Luck,luck that's all we can say for Rassie van der Dussen out there.
DRAMA! Broady Pody gets a wicket! No, Broady Pody does not get a wicket! What is happening? Rassie van der Dussen has been caught behind but Stuart Broad has overstepped!
Full delivery on middle, van der Dussen looks to flick it but gets hit on the pads.

BEATEN! What a delivery from Stuart Broad! How come that did not take the edge? Good length ball on off, nipping away, Rassie looks to defend but misses it altogether. Broad starts celebrating but sees that no one else is supporting him so he backs out.
On off, pushed to deep cover for a single.
On a length outside off, Elgar pushes it to deep cover and calls for a single.
Back of a length ball on middle, Dean blocks it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Poor bowling! Cannot bowl there at this pace. Short delivery on middle, Elgar camps back and pulls it to the deep square leg region for a boundary.
Good length ball on off, Elgar guides it to point.
Fullish delivery outside off, Dean leaves the ball alone.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

FIFTY! 14th one for Elgar in Tests. He has looked the only comfortable out there but he knows that it is only half the job done. Needs to continue to score a big one there and get his side closer to England's score. He gets there by guiding this length ball on off to point and taking a single.
Well fielded! Fullish delivery down the leg side, Elgar works it down to fine leg and picks up a couple to move to 49. Denly comes across and slides to clean it up.
Full delivery on off, Dean pushes it to cover.
Back of a length on off, Elgar stands tall and pushes it to point.
Full delivery outside off, Elgar lets the ball go to the keeper.
On off, Rassie defends it out.
FOUR! Sumptuous! Not a great delivery from Curran as well. Full delivery on off, van der Dussen lunges forward and creams the drive through extra cover for a boundary.
On middle, Rassie blocks it out onto the pitch.
Just short! Fuller one outside off, van der Dussen looks to push at it but it takes the outside edge. It goes on the bounce to the gully fielder.
Full delivery on middle and leg, Rassie flicks it to mid-wicket.
Back of a length on off, Elgar punches it to backward point and crosses over for a single.
On a length on off, Elgar pushes it to deep cover and will keep strike for the next over.
On off, defended to mid off.
FOUR! Valiant effort from Denly! Short of a length delivery down the leg side, Elgar just helps it on its way to fine leg. Denly comes across, dives but in the end the ball touches the ropes.
Fullish on middle, Elgar defends it back to the bowler.
Good length ball on middle, Elgar works it to mid-wicket.
Broad returns with a full delivery on off, Rassie pushes it to cover and crosses over for a single.
Stuart Broad will bowl from the other end. 6-4-12-2 are his figures.
On off, Dean defends it out.
Back of a length on off, Elgar taps it to gully.
FOUR! That is a fine, fine shot from Elgar. Curran dishes a half volley on middle, Elgar prods forward and creams the drive through mid on for the first boundary of the session.
Fullish on off, Elgar lunges forward and pushes it to cover.
Good length on middle, Elgar works it to backward square leg and picks up a couple.
Curran starts with a full delivery on middle, Elgar pushes it down to mid on.

The second session is all set to begin! Dean Elgar and Rassie van der Dussen make their way out to the middle to resume their innings. They still trail by 209 runs. The England players are also making their way out. Sam Curran will start for the visitors. Bowled just three overs in the first session.
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

South Africa, on the other hand, got the last wicket quickly but did not do justice with the bat at all. After a decent start from the openers, Pieter Malan was the first one to fall playing a shot to a one which he could left alone. Hamza and du Plessis soon followed him and the hosts were in tatters early on in the innings. They could have lost Rassie too but he survived due to an inside edge. Elgar has looked good and with van der Dussen, he will look to consolidate and stitch a big partnership. England though would look to bowl them out and get a big lead. What will happen? Will the Proteas fight back or will the visitors continue to chip away at the wickets? Join us in a while to find out.

England's session by a mile. They could not add much to their overnight score of 262/9 but their bowlers have been excellent in reply. They came out with a mission in hand and that was to pick up as many wickets as they can. Broad and Anderson did just that. The former started the procession with two quick wickets of Pieter Malan and Zubayr Hamza. Anderson then joined the party picking up the all-important wicket of Faf du Plessis. They could have had another wicket but an inside edge saved Rassie van der Dussen.
Full one outside off, Rassie van der Dussen lets the ball go to the keeper. LUNCH ON DAY 2.
On a length outside off, van der Dussen leaves it alone.
On middle, flicked to deep mid-wicket and a couple is taken before the fielder can clean it up.
BEATEN! What a ball from Stokes! Fuller one in the channel of uncertainty, moves away. Rassie looks to defend but misses it altogether.
Fuller one outside off, Rassie shoulders arms to this one.
Stokes starts with a good length ball on off, van der Dussen defends it off the back foot.
Ben Stokes is introduced into the attack.
Floats this one up on off, Elgar defends it out to point.

Fullish on middle, Elgar plays it down to long on for a single.
On off, defended off the front foot to cover.

Good length on middle, Elgar works it to the leg side and picks up a single.
On off, defended to cover.
The batsman has driven it through mid off.
Full delivery on off, pushed through covers for a couple.
Good length ball on off, Rassie pushes it to point and takes a single.

NOT OUT! Rassie van der Dussen is survived by a big inside edge. Full delivery on middle, van der Dussen looks to push but misses to get hit on the pads. There were two noises though. Anderson and the rest appeal. The umpire agrees and gives it out. Rassie has gone for the DRS straightaway. The Ultra Edge rolls in and it shows that there was an inside edge. The umpire will have to overturn his decision. Brilliant to review the on-field call. Had he missed, it would have been plumb.
Rassie van der Dussen. has been given out LBW and he has reviewed it immediately. If Rassie has not hit it, he is plumb. Let's see what happens.
On middle, Elgar solidly defends it back to the bowler.
Floated on off, pushed to cover for a single.
Flatter one on middle, van der Dussen defends it to short leg.
Looped up ball on off, Rassie prods forward and defends it out.

Flatter one outside off, Elgar leaves it alone.
Fullish ball outside off, van der Dussen makes a good leave to the keeper.

Good length ball on off, Rassie guides it to point.
Outside off, left alone.

BEATEN! That is a peach of a delivery. Good length delivery around off, moving away from the batsman. Rassie attempts to defend but it just whizzes past the outside edge of the bat and into the keeper's gloves.
Fullish delivery on off, Rassie defends it to cover.
Tosses this one up on middle, Elgar gently pushes it back to the bowler.

Looped up ball outside off, Elgar pushes it to cover.

Flatter delivery on middle and leg, van der Dussen works it to deep square leg and takes a single. 50 up for the Proteas.

EDGY FOUR! Things are happening here at Newlands. Fortunate way to get off the mark for van der Dussen. Back of a length ball outside off, Rassie pokes at it but gets a thick outside edge which goes between the second slip and the gully fielder. Stokes dives to his right but the ball goes quickly past him and into the fence.
Back of a length ball outside off, Rassie does not fiddle with it and lets it through to the keeper.
On a length outside off, moving in a bit. van der Dussen leaves it alone.

Flatter delivery on middle, Dean works it to mid-wicket.
On middle, played back to the bowler.
Floated ball on middle, Elgar works it to the leg side and says no for the single.
Loopy delivery on middle, Dean defends it out.

FOUR! UPPISH BUT SAFE! Bess starts with a floated ball outside off, Elgar lunges forward and looks to drive but it goes uppishly. Luckily for Elgar it goes wide of the diving fielder and into the extra cover fence. Not sure whether the fielder got his hand on it.
First signs of spin! Dominic Bess is into the attack.
On a length on middle, Rassie defends it out. Excellent over comes to an end from James Anderson.
Rassie van der Dussen is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Anderson returns and picks up the big fish, the South African skipper. Excellent bowling. Full delivery around off, du Plessis looks to defend but it takes the outside edge and goes to second slip. Stokes stationed there moves to his left and takes a simple catch. The hosts slip further. 40 for 3 in no time. Not the start South Africa would have wanted.
Good length outside off, du Plessis shoulders arms to this one.
Good length delivery with extra bounce. Faf looks to defend but it hits the splice of the bat and rolls onto the pitch.
On a length on middle, du Plessis blocks it back to the bowler.
Full delivery on middle, Faf defends it to mid on off the front foot.
James Anderson is back on.
On off, pushed to point for nothing.

Nicely bowled! Well played too. Very full delivery on middle, Elgar gets his bat down in time and blocks it out.
Good length ball on off, du Plessis blocks it out.
Outside off, left alone.

Good length on middle and leg, Elgar defends it to mid on.
Good length ball on middle, Faf defends it back to the bowler. Broad shows some aggression as he picks the ball and underarms the ball towards du Plessis. Stares exchanged.

Drinks! A brilliant hour for England then. After bundling out quickly, they have removed two Protea batters inside 10 overs. It is Stuart Broad who is doing the damage. Elgar has looked solid but his partners, not so good so far. Here's his skipper Faf du Plessis coming in to join him out in the middle. Can these two occupy the crease and build a decent stand together? An intriguing hour awaits.

OUT! CAUGHT! Excellent catch from Stokes and Broad gets his second wicket. South Africa are in a spot of bother. Back of a length ball outside off, nipping away. Hamza looks to defend it off the back foot but gets a thick outside edge towards second slip. Stokes there, dives to his right and pouches it just inches above the ground. Brilliant. Broad is making the ball talk from his end at Newlands.
Stuart Broad has got an official warning for running on the danger area. First one of the innings.
On a length on off, nipping in. Hamza defends it out solidly.
On off, driven towards mid off where the fielder dives and stops the ball. No run.
Good length ball on middle, Zubayr defends it out off the back foot.

FOUR! Brilliant shot from Hamza! Positive cricket! That's how he likes to play. Full delivery on off, Hamza leans forward and creams the drive through the cover region for a boundary. Stokes chases after it but does not manage to get there in time.
Full ball outside the off stump line, Dean lets the ball go to the keeper.
Fullish delivery on middle, Elgar works it to mid-wicket.
On off, Zubayr gets off the mark by guiding this towards point and taking a single.
Better from Curran! Good length ball outside off, Hamza leaves it alone.

Another one down the leg side, Elgar flicks it to the deep mid-wicket region and takes three before Crawley from deep square leg hares across and collects it. 7 from the first two balls to start with from Curran.
FOUR! Curran starts with a poor delivery on the pads, Elgar whips it away to the deep mid-wicket region for a boundary. The fielder from deep square leg comes across but gives up the chase.
First change from England. Sam Curran is brought into the attack. He picked up four wickets in the first innings of the first Test. Can he make an impact here as well?

BEATEN! Excellent. Just excellent stuff from Broad. Good length ball outside off, moving away from the batsman. Hamza looks to defend off the back foot but fails to get anything on it. A successful over comes to an end from Broad.
On off, Hamza pushes it back to Broad.
Length ball on off, Zubayr looks to defend but it goes off the outside edge towards gully who collects it on a bounce.
Good length ball on middle and leg, Hamza defends it out to mid on.
Fuller ball around off, Hamza comes forward and keeps it out.
Zubayr Hamza is the new man in.

OUT! Caught! Broad strikes and the debutant has to depart! Brilliant bowling from him. A slightly shortish ball outside off which shapes away after pitching. He can easily let this go to the keeper but this time he has a poke at it. The away movement means an outside edge is induced and it goes to Root at first slip. He takes it in front of his face nicely. Poor, poor shot this one from the debutant.

EDGY FOUR! Just short! Good length ball on off, nipping away, Elgar looks to defend it but gets squared up. It goes off the outside edge towards first slip. It bounces in front of him and goes between his legs into the fence.
Length ball on middle and leg, Elgar works it to deep square leg and picks up a couple.
Fuller ball on off, Elgar solidly defends it back to the bowler.
On a length on off, Elgar blocks it off the back foot to point.
Fullish delivery outside off, Dean shoulders arms to this one.
Good length ball on off, Elgar defends it to mid off.
Another leave to see off the over as Broad dishes out another good length ball outside off.
In the channel again but too wide to make Malan play. He shoulders arms.
Outside off this time, an easy leave for Malan.
Another ball around off on a fullish length, Malan pushes it to point.
Beauty from Broad! Fuller and just outside off. As Malan comes forward to defend the ball shapes away from his and bat. Luckily for him, it does not take the outside edge.
Good length ball on middle, blocked towards mid-wicket.
Nicely done! A fuller ball around off, Elgar runs it down through point and gully and before the fielder can get to the ball, a couple for him.
Around off, pushed to point.
On middle, Elgar pushes it to mid on.
Good length ball on off, Elgar waits and at the last moment taps it towards gully where the fielder does well to stop the ball with a tumble to his left.
Fuller and on middle, Elgar works it in front of square leg.
Good length ball on middle, worked towards square leg by Malan for a single.
Fuller and on off this time, Elgar looks to drive but gets an inside edge. The ball goes between his legs but luckily does not go onto the stumps.
Another one on off, Elgar once again makes a solid block.
This one is pitched on off and it comes into Elgar. He blocks it off the back foot.
He does that on this one. Bowls it around off and on a slightly fuller length, Elgar gets behind the line of the delivery and defends.
Another ball which is outside off, Elgar has nothing to do with it once again. Broad needs to get closer to the off pole and make Elgar play.
Shortish length ball outside off, Elgar makes a leave to start the over.
Gets slightly fuller and around off, Malan this time comes forward and defends it.
Make that third leave in a row as Malan once again covers his stumps and allows the ball to go to the keeper.
Another leave as Anderson bowls it on a good length ball outside off.
In the channel outside off, it is left alone.
Good length around off, tapped towards covers.
Outside off, Malan covers his stumps and lets it go to the keeper.
FOUR! This is a brilliant shot! Full and outside off, Elgar reaches out and drives it through point for another boundary.

FOUR BYES! That's through everyone. A good length ball which is once again angled into Elgar. He looks to defend but the ball comes back in sharply to beat his inside edge. Buttler behind the wicket fails to collect the ball either. It goes behind him and into the fence.
Landed around off on a good length, Elgar looks to defend but the ball takes the inner half of the bat and goes to square leg.
Good length ball outside off, it is angled into the left-hander. Elgar covers his stumps and shoulders arms.
FOUR! Punched nicely! First one from Elgar's bat. Another fuller ball around off, Elgar just punches it on the front foot. It races to the long off fence in a jiffy.
Fuller ball on off first up from Broad. Elgar leans and pushes it to mid off.
Stuart Broad with the ball from the other end. 2 slips and a gully for him.

FOUR! First runs for Pieter Malan in Test cricket! This will give him a lot of confidence. Short delivery outside off, Malan stands tall and punches it through the cover region for a boundary. Gives a smile after hitting that shot.
Fullish ball nipping away, Pieter leaves the ball alone to the keeper.
Full delivery on middle, Malan defends his first ball in international cricket back to the bowler.
South Africa and Elgar are underway! Fuller one outside off, Elgar pushes it through covers and crosses over for a single.
Back of a length ball on off, Elgar defends it out to point.
Anderson starts with a good length ball on middle, Elgar defends it out to mid off.
